text: Hoping to get the treasure for himself at last. <break time="0.8s" /> Tom went back to the swamp. <break time="0.8s" /> And found the dark woodsman strolling along. <break time="0.8s" /> With his axe on his shoulder. <break time="0.8s" /> This time Tom agreed to the bargain. <break time="0.8s" /> But there was one condition. <break time="0.8s" /> That the treasure must be used. <break time="0.8s" /> In the devils service. <break time="0.8s" /> The devil first suggested a slave ship. <break time="0.8s" /> But Tom refused. <break time="0.8s" /> For wicked as he was even the devil could not tempt him. <break time="0.8s" /> To become a slave trader. <break time="0.8s" /> Then the devil proposed. <break time="0.8s" /> That Tom become a usurer. <break time="0.8s" /> A moneylender who charges very high interest. <break time="0.8s" /> And this was exactly to Toms taste. <break time="0.8s" /> You shall lend money. <break time="0.8s" /> At two percent a month. <break time="0.8s" /> Said the devil. <break time="0.8s" /> And Tom eagerly replied. <break time="0.8s" /> That he would charge four. <break time="0.8s" /> Within a few days. <break time="0.8s" /> Tom was seated behind a desk in Boston. <break time="0.8s" /> At a time when money was scarce. <break time="0.8s" /> And many people badly needed loans. <break time="0.8s" /> He grew rich quickly. <break time="0.8s" /> And in proportion to the distress. <break time="0.8s" /> Of each borrower. <break time="0.8s" /> Was the hardness of his terms. <break time="0.8s" /> As Tom grew old, however. <break time="0.8s" /> He began to worry about his bargain. <break time="0.8s" /> And he suddenly became. <break time="0.8s" /> A loud and eager churchgoer. <break time="0.8s" /> He always carried a small Bible in his coat pocket. <break time="0.8s" /> Hoping that it would protect him. <break time="0.8s" /> If the devil ever came to collect.
